title: The Probabilistic Foundations of Surveillance Failure: From False Alerts to Structural Bias
reasoning: The paper is a theoretical study of probabilistic limits in high-dimensional surveillance and screening systems. It uses statistical modeling (Poisson approximations, large deviations theory) to explain 'structural bias' as a mathematical consequence of differential exposure. It does not evaluate, benchmark, or discuss religion, faith, morals, or ethical frameworks in the sense of moral reasoning or theological analysis.
